title: Authors have mixed feelings about the $1.5 billion Anthropic copyright infringement settlement
summary: Some say the $3,100 per title payout is small compensation for what they view as big, ongoing threats from the makers of generative AI models.
full_text:
Authors have mixed feelings about the $1.5 billion Anthropic copyright infringement settlement
Charles Graeber said he has some positive feelings about being among the three main plaintiffs in one of the largest copyright infringement settlements in history.
"I was proud to be part of a group that showed that a ragtag bunch of authors joined later by publishers could actually hold together as a class, face a Goliath like Anthropic and get a meaningful number out of them," The New York Times bestselling author and journalist told NPR.
But he's also hesitant to call the efforts and outcome of the lawsuit an all-out win.
Graeber is among the more than 300,000 writers involved in the suit who may soon be getting a modest windfall. A federal judge in San Francisco rubber stamped a $1.5 billion settlement in July resulting from a landmark class action lawsuit the authors brought against the AI company Anthropic two years ago.
The AI company agreed to settle after a federal judge ruled last year that it had used the contents of millions of digitized copyrighted books to train the large language models behind its chatbot, Claude, without seeking the consent of or compensating the authors of those works.
Graeber said he is entitled to around $3,100 in compensation for each of the two books he wrote that were used to feed Claude, including The New York Times bestselling true crime book The Good Nurse, which Netflix adapted into a movie in 2022.
The author said the hard cash reaffirms that piracy is a crime. But he has mixed feelings about the last 2-plus years he's spent fighting Anthropic. "A lot of travel, a lot of discussion about what to do and how to proceed and a lot of jobs passed up," he said. "I'm much poorer for this settlement, ironically."
The overall settlement amount may seem large. But thousands of authors are involved, and they have to split the money with the publishers. Also, more than $100 million went to the plaintiffs' lawyers.
And perhaps more importantly, the case could be seen as more of a win for the AI companies than it is for the publishing industry.
A win for the AI industry?
That's because within the narrow terms of this particular lawsuit, the court did not find it illegal for Anthropic to train its AI algorithms on authors' copyrighted works – as long as the company pays for the books it uses.
"Training AI on books is fair use under copyright law," said Aparna Sridhar, deputy general counsel for Anthropic, in a statement to NPR. "More than 91% of authors and publishers covered by the settlement have claimed their share of the payment, and we're looking forward to bringing this matter to a close." The company declined to respond to further questions about the implications of the judge's ruling.
A federal judge also ruled in favor of Meta in a similar case last year involving a group of authors, who included Richard Kadrey and Sarah Silverman. The authors sued Meta, alleging they used pirated copies of their novels to train some of its AI models. Meta claimed fair use and won because the authors failed to present evidence that the tech company's use of their books affected the market for their original work.
AI companies often invoke the fair use doctrine – which enables the use of copyrighted works without the copyright holder's consent in some situations – as they try to make the case in court for training their models on these materials.
New York Times bestselling author Andrea Bartz, another named plaintiff in the Anthropic trial alongside Graeber, said the argument for fair use makes little sense when the algorithms are being used to create machine-authored texts that directly compete with works by human authors on the open market.
"The algorithm is being used to essentially try to put us out of a job," Bartz said.
Threats from abroad
Meanwhile, even if laws in the U.S. eventually give authors stronger copyright protections, there's no guarantee that other countries will play by the same rules.
Intellectual property lawyer Dale Nelson, who was not involved in the Anthropic vs Bartz case but said she follows such matters closely, notes the threat from overseas AI companies, especially the creators of powerful and increasingly popular chatbots like China's DeepSeek.
"The government in China controls in large part what the companies are doing," Nelson said. "So I think that enforcement attempts there would be very difficult."
Bartz said to address this reality, AI regulation needs to move beyond borders, especially as nations compete for political dominance through AI.
Chinese AI companies often use a technique to build their models called "AI distillation." This involves feeding their models the outputs generated by other AI models, often high-quality U.S.-based ones like OpenAI's GPT-4 or Anthropic's Claude, instead of directly training them on pirated copies of books by American authors.
"The only thing that makes sense to me is sort of this non-proliferation agreement, this treaty that could be extended internationally," said Bartz.
But despite the threats, Bartz said she is optimistic about the proliferation of copyright infringement cases involving AI working their way through the U.S. court system, and said authors must keep fighting for their rights.
"My hope is that this lawsuit is the first of many steps that will create a more fair environment for creatives in the era of AI," she said.
Licensing – a possible way forward?
One possible way for authors to get a fairer shake in the age of AI could be through the licensing of their work to AI companies.
"Licensing is a way to make sure that training happens legally," said Umair Kazi, director of policy and advocacy at the nonprofit group, Authors Guild. "Not only that, licensing also enables rights holders to restrict how their works show up in AI chatbot outputs. Maybe you license just for the training, but you don't want the model churning out summaries or other kinds of derivative works – sequels and the likes."
There are already some such deals between publishers and AI companies in place, such as Perplexity AI's agreement with media entities like the Los Angeles Times and Le Monde to license content for the training of its models. There are also online licensing marketplaces, such as Created by Humans.
But it remains to be seen if licensing will take off.
"Because the big AI companies are all in litigation over training, licensing deals are still rare," Kazi said.

title: With rapid Ebola aid, China shows itself a reliable partner of Africa
summary:
When Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), met Jiang Feng, head of China’s mission to the African Union, in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in mid-July, the message was practical. They signed a handover certificate that brought Beijing’s direct emergency support for the Ebola response to US$4.5 million. A five-member Chinese medical team was already working in the Democratic Republic of Congo capital of Kinshasa.
Kaseya described the contribution as...
full_text:
With rapid Ebola aid, China shows itself a reliable partner of Africa
Public health now sits beside trade, infrastructure and digital connectivity as a core part of Africa-China ties
Kaseya described the contribution as a strong signal of solidarity. What matters is how quickly that solidarity becomes money, equipment and people on the ground.
Disease outbreaks reveal partnerships with unusual clarity. Ports can be opened, trade figures celebrated and agreements signed. An Ebola alert asks a harder question: can a partner release funds, send experts and move supplies while health ministries are still tracing contacts?
So whom does Africa call when a dangerous test result arrives at midnight?
For a growing number of governments, China is among the first they call. Over the past decade, Beijing has moved beyond being a builder of roads, railways and power plants. It has also become a practical partner in public health emergencies.
Trade access and infrastructure finance may bring governments together, yet health cooperation reaches into laboratories, hospitals and communities. Here, state capacity is measured in days rather than decades. China’s response to the Ebola outbreak offers a clear example.

title: So how do you get access to the Qantas chairman’s lounge? Alan Joyce has some tips
summary:
In his memoir, the former Qantas chief executive denies using the lounge as a tool to influence politicians

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Judges, politicians, newspaper editors and big spenders: Alan Joyce, the former Qantas chief executive, has revealed how the airline admits members to its private chairman’s lounge.

In his memoir, released on Tuesday, Joyce denies using the lounge as a tool to influence politicians and claims famous Australians “begged” to be granted access to “arguably the most exclusive club in the country”.

Continue reading...
full_text:
Judges, politicians, newspaper editors and big spenders: Alan Joyce, the former Qantas chief executive, has revealed how the airline admits members to its private chairman’s lounge.
In his memoir, released on Tuesday, Joyce denies using the lounge as a tool to influence politicians and claims famous Australians “begged” to be granted access to “arguably the most exclusive club in the country”.
The Irish-born Joyce was one of the airline’s longest-serving heads, leading the company from 2008 until his resignation in 2023.
He has previously described the lounge as a “commercial arrangement” but the comments in his memoir, Riding the Jet Stream, provide his most expansive explanation of how access to the luxury private zone in Australia’s major airports operates.
Joyce writes that neither he nor the Qantas chair personally handled invitations to the lounge and had only occasional input.
Membership of the “invitation-only” club was approved by a small group of senior executives, he says.
The “core” membership included “federal politicians, most state politicians, high court and federal judges, editors of national newspapers, a few journalists, and high-profile celebrities”.
Companies that spent about $1m each year on Qantas flights “likely” received one lounge membership each, which could be rotated between executives, Joyce writes.
In 2023 the company told a Senate inquiry it also extended invitations to secretaries and deputy secretaries of federal departments, agency chairs, chief executives and commissioners.
Qantas has been contacted for comment.
‘You cannot buy your way in’
In his book, Joyce writes that the company once had to rescind memberships after numbers grew “out of control”, due to “inconsistent oversight”, though he does not specify when that occurred.
Qantas also maintained control of membership by requiring “high standards of conduct”, he writes. Joyce gives the example of Jacqui Lambie, who was banned from the airline for six months after a “rant” in the Melbourne chairman’s lounge, for which she apologised.
Membership feels “elite” and discreet due to the exclusivity, rather than the perks, Joyce writes.
“You cannot buy your way in, and no amount of frequent-flyer points will get you a spot,” he writes.
Free, on-demand fine food and alcohol and comfortable facilities are available at the private lounges. Membership also gives customers free seat selection and priority for customer service, airport check-in and security, baggage handling and upgrade requests, according to the Qantas website.
A number of politicians have handed back their membership of the lounge in recent years.
In his memoir, Joyce denies claims that Qantas exercised influence through lounge membership, describing it as “the wildest assertion”.
“If that were true, Qantas would never have lost a case in the High Court or Federal Court – yet we did,” Joyce writes.
He writes that the lounge was a relationship tool, not a lever of control.
The memoir also contains Joyce’s first public comments on claims he acceded to Anthony Albanese’s requests for free upgrades on Qantas flights, which the prime minister denied in 2024.
“I have no recollection of ever receiving a call from the Prime Minister or his staff requesting an upgrade,” Joyce writes.
Joyce says his standard practice for such requests, which “politicians from all major parties” had made, would have been to tell his personal assistant to arrange the upgrade.
But Joyce says he never asked his assistant nor was there any record of him authorising such an upgrade for Albanese.
“It’s bunkum, but nothing grabs a voter’s attention quite like suggesting a pollie has their nose in the proverbial trough,” he writes.

full_text:
X Money, a core part of Elon Musk’s mission to turn X into an “everything app,” is rolling out starting today, 9to5Mac reports. The payment platform offers a digital wallet and peer-to-peer payments similar to Venmo, along with a metal Visa card users can emblazon with their X username. Other perks include Apple Wallet support and free money transfers on X. It also advertises “up to” a 6 percent APY, but only Premium Plus subscribers are eligible for it — standard Premium subscribers have to deposit a certain amount of money to get a “boosted” 6 percent APY.
X Money is launching in the US starting today
Elon Musk’s payment platform is rolling out first to X Premium and Premium Plus subscribers.
Elon Musk’s payment platform is rolling out first to X Premium and Premium Plus subscribers.
X Money was previously limited to an invite-only beta, but will now be available to X Premium and Premium Plus subscribers in the US. The launch comes a few months after Elon Musk said “early public access” for the payment platform was launching in April.
Earlier this year, Senator Elizabeth Warren raised safety concerns about X Money, writing that it could pose risks to “consumers, our national security, and the stability of the financial system.” Launching a payment platform on X has been a mission of Musk’s for a while now — in 2023, he said during an X staff meeting that, “If it involves money, it’ll be on our platform.”

summary: Gaming keyboards have evolved over the years to add RGB LEDs, extra knobs, and buttons with screens, but one feature has remained fairly consistent: the mechanical switch. That’s slowly changing, with brands introducing adjustable optical switches that are more customizable and have a faster response time. Razer’s Huntsman V3 Pro TKL is a compact, wired […]
full_text:
Gaming keyboards have evolved over the years to add RGB LEDs, extra knobs, and buttons with screens, but one feature has remained fairly consistent: the mechanical switch. That’s slowly changing, with brands introducing adjustable optical switches that are more customizable and have a faster response time. Razer’s Huntsman V3 Pro TKL is a compact, wired option on sale at Amazon for $124.99 (usually $159.99).
Razer’s analog Huntsman V3 Pro is over 20 percent off
This discounted gaming keyboard features customizable analog switches and advanced features for competitive gamers.
This discounted gaming keyboard features customizable analog switches and advanced features for competitive gamers.
Optical switches constantly read the height of each key, opening up a wealth of new features that traditional mechanical switches don’t support. For example, you can set the activation height for different keys, down to 0.1mm for the lightest touch, or up to 4mm for keys you don’t want to accidentally press at the wrong time, and they can reset without reaching the top height for faster repeated presses.
Like some other keyboards with optical switches, you can use a function Razer calls “Snap Tap” to prioritize specific key inputs over each other, letting you rock back and forth between your strafing keys in a shooter, for example. The feature is turned off by default, and is banned in some games like Counter-Strike 2, but can be switched on at the keyboard level or in the Razer Synapse app.

title: U.S. Senate puts off crypto Clarity Act for now as it focuses limited bandwidth elsewhere
full_text:
U.S. Senate puts off crypto Clarity Act for now as it focuses limited bandwidth elsewhere
The majority leader is pursuing floor time for unrelated bills as the crypto industry waits for its policy effort to get its chance for votes.
- The U.S. Senate will move on to a couple of other matters while lawmakers debate the details of the crypto Clarity Act, according to a schedule set out by Majority Leader John Thune to first pursue nominations and a Russia sanctions bill.
- The Clarity Act could still get some preliminary Senate action next week, though that’s the final week before the chamber begins its summer recess, potentially shifting Clarity’s next window to September.
The U.S. Senate has shelved the crypto Digital Asset Market Clarity Act for the moment as it proceeds with different bills on Russian sanctions and federal nominations, further setting aside the industry's central policy effort and reducing its available runway in a crowded Senate agenda.
Majority Leader John Thune started pursuing a package of nominees on Monday and expected to shift to a Russia sanctions bill Tuesday night, at which point he's set to start its cloture process. The arcane Senate procedure to manage bill debates involves a number of steps and waiting periods before legislation typically get to a final vote, and the chamber's procedures generally limit it to one disputed bill at a time. That means it's unlikely the body can move on the Clarity Act before the other matters get sorted or expire, which could take days.
The Russia bill would impose sanctions on the country's leadership and tariffs for trading partners, and it's dedicated now to the recently deceased senator who supported it, Lindsey Graham. Plus, Graham's funeral this week will occupy the chamber's attention Tuesday and Wednesday, in Washington and South Carolina.
Bottom line: Clarity isn't likely to come up for voting before next week — the final days before the chamber's summer break is set to start on August 8. The hotly debated market structure bill isn't yet ready for a vote, anyway, as the parties continue to try to seek a compromise on a contentious provision that's stood in the way of a deal: the ban against senior government officials, including President Donald Trump, backing crypto projects.
Thune's office had told CoinDesk last week that his next floor-time priority would go to the Russia legislation. While the majority leader also said he hopes to get to Clarity before the break, he said the leadership would have to "see where the votes are."
At this point in the Senate calendar, every hour of floor time is a precious commodity, and the debate over the Clarity Act still hasn't settled some of the major outstanding points — especially the section on government ethics, which was the topic of a Monday event hosted by Democrats opposing the Clarity Act and the president's crypto activities.
Having significant disagreements at this stage could narrow the chances that Clarity can become law in 2026, potentially throwing the industry into some uncertainty over the timeline for U.S. regulations. If this legislation tanks, the next best avenues for regulatory legitimacy is the ongoing implementation of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act and the policy efforts at the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
In the Senate, the best hope for the industry at this point may be get its own preliminary push into the cloture process just before the lawmakers scatter on their recess.
Though a similar version of the Clarity Act had already advanced in the House of Representatives, the Senate has tended to be the greater bottleneck for legislative progress. In this case, it was initially hung up for months on the debate between the crypto sector and bankers on the treatment of stablecoin yield, which resulted in a compromise that limited stablecoin rewards programs to formats that wouldn't resemble (and compete with) yield-bearing bank deposits. Then the debate shifted toward the crypto limits on government officials.
Last week, that ethics section reached a potential breakthrough with an agreement from Trump that he'd accept the provision to limit his interactions with digital assets. While White House officials touted the historic, unprecedented ethics constraints, Democrats quickly countered that the restrictions didn't go far enough to curtail Trump's lucrative crypto empire. Still, both sides agreed to keep talking.
The House and Senate both return for a few weeks in September. But that's the end of the available floor time. And after the November elections, Congress will enter its so-called lame duck session in which defeated and retiring lawmakers will be serving out their final weeks until the next session of Congress begins in January. Lame duck sessions sometimes produce legislation in what can be a chaotic period of desperate dealmaking, though they can also lock up with political paralysis.
Even if the Clarity Act passes in the Senate, it must return for another approval in the House, where recent infighting among Republicans has gotten in the way of action on other initiatives. But if it clears both sides of Congress, it can head to Trump's desk to be signed into law.
In recent weeks, the president had refused to sign an unrelated bipartisan housing bill, because he's taken a stand against all legislation until lawmakers send him a bill that demands new voter-identification requirements before the midterms. He's actively called for the Clarity Act to be completed, though it's unclear whether it'll get a free pass. Either way, after a 10-day period of inaction from the president, an approved bill would automatically become law.

title: Kalshi, Polymarket win pause against Minnesota's prediction market ban
full_text:
Kalshi, Polymarket win pause against Minnesota's prediction market ban
A federal judge ruled that Minnesota's law criminalizing prediction markets would probably violate the federal Commodity Exchange Act.
A federal judge ruled that Minnesota’s law banning prediction markets likely runs afoul of the Commodity Exchange Act, granting a preliminary injunction against the law to Kalshi, Polymarket and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
Judge Katherine Menendez, of the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota, ruled Monday that Minnesota’s recently passed law that would ban prediction market operators from offering their products in the state seems to be preempted by the federal CEA, and that the companies and federal regulator “are likely to succeed” in showing so after a full trial.
Kalshi, Polymarket and the CFTC sued Minnesota earlier this year after the state passed the law criminalizing the operation of prediction markets, arguing that the statute violated the CFTC’s jurisdiction to oversee “swaps,” which prediction market contracts are structured as.
In her ruling, Judge Menendez said that the three parties had shown they were likely to succeed in their arguments that the law underpinning U.S. commodities exchanges preempts the state law, that the CFTC has jurisdiction over these products and that the plaintiffs would likely succeed on the merits of the case.
“The Court finds that Plaintiffs have met their burden to show they are likely to succeed on the merits of their express-preemption claims, at least as to the application of Minnesota’s law to many of the trades listed on Kalshi’s and Polymarket US’s platforms,” the ruling said. “Specifically, it appears that whether the Minnesota statute is expressly preempted turns on whether the state law attempts to regulate trades in event contracts that qualify as ‘swaps’ within the meaning of the CEA.”
Some of the contracts on prediction markets might fit within the Minnesota law, the judge said, pointing to predictions about who might win the TV program “Love Island” as an example, but it would be difficult to target a preliminary injunction just to those issues.
Not granting a halt of the law would also cause “irreparable harm” to Kalshi and Polymarket, the ruling added.
The preliminary injunction will last until “a final decision on the merits is reached,” the judge said.

title: Hong Kong prepares banks for quantum threats amid tokenization push
summary: The HKMA aims to make Hong Kong’s banking sector fully prepared for quantum-related security risks by 2030 as the city expands tokenized finance.
full_text:
Hong Kong prepares banks for quantum threats amid tokenization push
The HKMA aims to make Hong Kong’s banking sector fully prepared for quantum-related security risks by 2030 as the city expands tokenized finance.
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has launched a framework to assess banks’ preparedness for quantum-computing threats as the city expands its use of tokenized deposits, digital assets and blockchain settlement.
On Monday, the HKMA introduced a white paper on quantum preparedness and the sector’s first Quantum Preparedness Index (QPI). The index gave the sector an overall readiness score of 2.3 out of 10, while the white paper found that around half of surveyed institutions had no formal post-quantum planning in place. The HKMA said it aims to achieve full sector readiness, represented by a QPI score of 10, by 2030.
The development comes as Hong Kong moves more traditional financial activity onto distributed ledgers. Government figures show that Hong Kong has issued three batches of tokenized green bonds totaling about HK$16.8 billion (about $2.1 billion) since 2023, while the HKMA is advancing tokenized deposits and digital-asset settlement through Project Ensemble.
The HKMA white paper said distributed ledger applications and payment networks depend on cryptography for core functions and could face severe disruption if those protections were compromised.
It also said one surveyed institution completed a proof of concept applying post-quantum cryptography to distributed-ledger connectivity and cited HSBC’s 2024 use of quantum-safe technology to move tokenized gold across distributed ledgers.
Hong Kong’s tokenization push raises quantum stakes
The quantum initiative follows the launch of the HKMA’s Fintech 2030 strategy in 2025, which made tokenization one of four strategic pillars in a plan comprising more than 40 initiatives.
The regulator said it would accelerate real-world asset (RWA) tokenization, regularize tokenized government bond issuance and explore tokenized Exchange Fund papers, with blockchain settlement supported by e-HKD, tokenized deposits and regulated stablecoins.
Related: Hong Kong launches initiative to help banks with DLT adoption
In a Feb. 11, 2026, speech, Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan said banks in Hong Kong held more than HK$14 billion (about $1.785 billion) in digital assets under custody at the end of 2025, up about 180% year over year, while tokenized deposits had reached HK$29 billion ($3.7 billion).
According to the HKMA white paper, quantum computers capable of running Shor’s algorithm at scale could eventually break widely used RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography. This could allow attackers to decrypt protected data or forge the digital signatures used to authorize transactions, verify identities and establish trust in financial systems.
Because replacing embedded cryptographic systems can take years, the HKMA urged banks to begin inventories, risk assessments and migration planning before such machines become available.

title: Binance phishs its own staff monthly, India censors BitChat code: Asia Express
summary: Binance has been phishing its own staff to get ahead of potential attacks. South Korean crypto volumes tank 89% — plus all of the week’s other crypto news from Asia.
full_text:
Binance phishs its own staff monthly, India censors BitChat code: Asia Express
Binance has been phishing its own staff to get ahead of potential attacks. South Korean crypto volumes tank 89% — plus all of the week’s other crypto news from Asia.
Binance ‘red teams’ its own staff every month to keep hackers out
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has been running simulated phishing attacks against its own employees for the past four years and can fire staff who repeatedly fail the tests, according to Binance chief security officer Jimmy Su.
The fake attacks are conducted by Binance’s red team, an internal ethical hacking unit whose job is to break into systems to identify vulnerabilities.
“We do phishing attacks on our own employees on a monthly basis just so we understand if our security hygiene is improving,” Su told Cointelegraph. “The ones that have failed it, we will do remediation training.”
In February, AMLBot estimated that 65% of crypto security incidents in 2025 were driven by social engineering.
India’s BitChat GitHub takedown order ‘unconstitutional’
India’s Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) has condemned a government order directing GitHub to remove repositories for Jack Dorsey’s decentralized messaging app BitChat, calling the move unconstitutional and warning it threatens free speech and open-source software.
The statement came a day after India’s cybercrime agency ordered GitHub to disable access to three BitChat repositories within three hours, saying the decentralized messaging app could be used to bypass internet shutdowns, evade lawful surveillance and facilitate unlawful activities.
BitChat is a decentralized messaging app that routes encrypted messages between nearby devices over Bluetooth without relying on internet connectivity or centralized servers.
Since its release in July 2025, the app has gained traction during periods of unrest and internet outages in countries including Madagascar, Nepal, Uganda, Jamaica and Iran.
More crypto news from India:
— India’s Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has issued guidance directing crypto exchanges to report all transactions on their platforms to the Income Tax department.
Balaji’s Network School turns to Kazakhstan amid Malaysian setback
Balaji Srinivasan’s utopian Network School looks set to move to Kazakhstan after Malaysian authorities revoked its business license over alleged premises-use violations.
A memorandum of understanding was signed between Kazakhstan’s Minister of Digital Development and Srinivasan to establish a campus in the country which has been positioning itself as an emerging technology hub, and has plans for Central Asia’s first “crypto city” in Alatau.
The Network School had been at the centre of a scandal involving hosting Israeli citizens given the Muslim majority country has no diplomatic relations with Israel. The US State Department called in the Malaysian envoy to ask for an explanation about the country’s apparent policy of deporting dual citizens with Israeli passports. 
Source: The Times of Israel/Reuters
South Korea crypto volumes shrink as retail investors shift to stocks
South Korea’s five major crypto exchanges have seen their combined trading activity fall by 89% year over year, even as the country’s stock market surged.
The Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) benchmark more than doubled over the period, while volumes across the country’s largest won-based crypto platforms fell off a cliff.
Cointelegraph reviewed CoinGecko’s historical 24-hour volume readings for Upbit, Bithumb, Coinone, Korbit and Gopax, comparing seven-day periods in July 2025 and July 2026.
On a combined basis, average daily volume fell about 89%, to $305 million from $2.82 billion in the comparable July 2025 period. 
More crypto news from Korea:
— South Korean crypto exchange Korbit will reportedly rebrand as Digital X after becoming part of Mirae Asset Group.
— South Korea’s KB Kookmin Bank will launch a blockchain-based cross-border payment service for import and export businesses in August using JPMorgan’s Kinexys network.
— South Korean regulators have removed 29 unlicensed crypto exchange apps from the Google Play store. Affected apps include those from OKX, Bybit, MEXC, Kucoin, Gemini, Backpack, and BitMEX.
— North Korean authorities have reportedly arrested a group of former state cyber operators and IT specialists accused of hacking two state banks and laundering stolen funds through cryptocurrency.
Thailand SEC files complaint against Bitkub over alleged false disclosures
Thailand’s SEC filed a criminal complaint against Bitkub and two former directors over alleged false disclosures linked to a 2021 cyberattack involving $50 million in assets.
The complaint names former Bitkub directors Sakolkorn Sakavee and Thaweesap Rawan, who the SEC said were responsible for submitting company reports during the period under investigation.
The case comes as Bitkub’s parent company considers a potential public listing, putting renewed attention on transparency and governance at one of Thailand’s most prominent crypto businesses.
More crypto news from Thailand:
— Thailand’s Kbank has signed a memorandum of understanding with BPMG and HashKey Group to develop stablecoin-based cross-border remittance services.
— Thailand authorities have raided seven illegal Bitcoin mining operations after uncovering large scale electricity theft. More than 1900 crypto mining machines were seized.
One of two Bitcoin mining warehouses in Samut Sakhon alleged to be stealing power. Source: DSI Facebook page.
Philippine bank BPI plans stablecoin payments pilot
The Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) is planning to pilot a stablecoin-based settlement rail for cross-border payments to freelancers, virtual assistants and other workers receiving overseas income.
Developed with global digital clearinghouse Meridian, the system is intended to reduce the cost and processing time of inbound payments while retaining safeguards used in traditional banking transactions, according to ABS-CBN and the Philippine Daily Inquirer.
Stablecoins would be used as a settlement instrument before the funds are converted to Philippine pesos and credited to recipients’ BPI accounts.
Coinbase to expand Singapore office headcount by 25%: Report
Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase plans to expand its presence in Singapore and grow its headcount from 150 to about 200 staff members by the end of 2026.
The cryptocurrency exchange is mainly looking to hire more engineers, customer service, relationship management staff and institutional sales representatives for its Singapore office, which opened at One Raffles Quay on Wednesday. 
Hassan Ahmed, Coinbase’s country director for Singapore, told the Business Times the exchange plans to expand its operations in Singapore because the city state is increasingly becoming a strategic hub for cryptocurrency innovation.
More Singapore crypto news:
— The Singapore Police Force and the U.S. FBI signed a memorandum of understanding to strengthen joint operations on online scams including crypto related scams, cyber fraud, and money laundering cases.
— Singapore based payments firm Triple-A reportedly lost $11.8 million after its hot wallet was drained. The firm said it was investigating but no customer funds were affected.
— The Monetary Authority of Singapore has tightened monetary policy, which will lead to the Singapore dollar appreciating by about 1% per year.
Hong Kong crypto giant HashKey merges regional exchange into one
Hong Kong digital asset services business HashKey Holdings has merged its HashKey Exchange and HashKey Global exchanges into a single platform and application.
Core jurisdictional hubs including Hong Kong, Singapore, the Middle East (Dubai) and Bermuda have been merged under a single platform.
The idea is that all users download the same application wherever they are, while the platform manages compliance on the back end with local regulatory frameworks.

full_text:
What Is a Digital Commodity?
We'd love your feedback.
A digital commodity is an onchain asset that draws its value from open-market supply and demand rather than from the work of a company or central issuer.
Assets in this category are freely transferable and traded on public markets, which makes them behave more like traditional commodities such as gold than like a share of company stock. Bitcoin is the clearest example of a digital commodity.
In the United States, "digital commodity" has become a specific regulatory label that helps decide which government agency oversees a given digital asset. As the cryptocurrency market grows, the boundary between a commodity and a security has become one of the central questions in crypto policy.
In this article, we’ll cover the importance of this distinction and some major examples of digital commodities.
What is a Digital Commodity?
A digital commodity is a digital asset that functions similarly to a traditional commodity. Its value is not dependent on any particular company or business, but rather by supply and demand forces on the open market.
The absence of a central issuer is what separates a digital commodity from a security, such as a share of stock. A stock represents a claim on a company, and its price moves based on the company's performance, while a digital commodity such as bitcoin has no issuer to report earnings or pay dividends, so it acts like a tradable good.
Key Characteristics of Digital Commodities
There are several key characteristics that define a “digital commodity”, some of which include:
- Fungibility: One unit can be freely transferred or traded with another asset without any restrictions.
- Decentralization: No single party can control the asset, making its value entirely dependent on market dynamics.
As crypto markets grew over the years, regulators had to figure out how crypto assets should be treated. Since certain assets had similar characteristics to traditional commodities rather than assets like stocks or bonds, they were categorized as legally similar.
There were long-standing questions on which specific digital assets were considered commodities or securities. These categories are overseen by different regulatory bodies in the United States: the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) or the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), respectively.
The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, a proposed U.S. cryptocurrency market structure bill, would create a formal statutory definition of "digital commodity." It defines the term as a digital asset that draws its value from the use of a blockchain rather than from a company. And it would only grant that status once a network is decentralized enough to run without a controlling group.
Examples of Digital Commodities
Bitcoin (BTC)
Bitcoin is the largest cryptocurrency and the one most often described as a digital commodity, as it runs on a decentralized network with no central issuer. Its supply is capped at 21 million coins and released on a fixed schedule set in code, giving it a scarcity model similar to a traditional mined commodity, such as gold.
U.S. regulators have reflected this view for years. The CFTC labelled bitcoin a commodity in 2015, with the SEC following suit in 2026.
Ethereum (ETH)
Ether (ETH) is the second-largest cryptocurrency by market cap. It is the native asset of Ethereum, a decentralized blockchain network that enables developers to build programmable applications.
There has historically been more debate on ETH’s status as a security as opposed to a commodity. This is because it was initially sold via a pre-sale in 2014, a structure that resembles a securities offering.
However, the SEC declared ETH a digital commodity alongside bitcoin in 2026. Their explanation was that while its initial token sale may be “securities-esque” due to the promise of profit, the token can trade as a commodity once those promises are met or abandoned and token holders no longer depend on the creators' work.
Other Digital Commodities
The SEC and CFTS 2026 joint interpretive release named 16 tokens as examples of digital commodities. Alongside BTC and ETH, the non-exhaustive list included Solana, XRP, Cardano, Chainlink, Avalanche, Polkadot, Hedera, Stellar, Litecoin, Dogecoin, Shiba Inu, Tezos, Bitcoin Cash, and Aptos.
How Digital Commodities Differ From Traditional Commodities
Traditional commodities are physical goods such as gold, silver, oil, and wheat. They are traditionally stored in vaults or warehouses and are also traded on spot and futures markets.
Digital and traditional commodities are both valued based on supply and demand dynamics and are tradeable on futures markets that enable traders to hedge or speculate on their prices. They are also not representations of ownership in any company, which is why both sit outside the definition of a security.
One of the main differences between the two is their form. A traditional commodity is a tangible, physical good, such as bars of gold or barrels of oil. A digital commodity is lines of code and numbers on a blockchain that do not physically exist.
Because of this, physical commodities are slow, having to rely on physical deliveries and traditional processes. On the other hand, digital commodities can move any time, anywhere, with no centralized intermediaries, within seconds.
Digital Commodity vs Security
A security represents an investment in a common enterprise, with profit expected from the efforts of others. Examples include company stocks, bonds and, investment contracts. U.S. courts assess whether something qualifies as a security using the Howey test, which essentially asks the question of whether people invested in a common enterprise expect profit from the work of others.
In the U.S., securities are registered with the SEC and carry heavier obligations than commodities, such as having to publish detailed disclosures and meet reporting requirements meant to protect investors. A commodity faces lighter requirements.
Whether an asset is a security or commodity determines where it can be listed, the rules behind how investors are protected, as well as which agency can enforce those rules.
Who Regulates Digital Commodities?
The Role of the CFTC
The CFTC is the U.S. agency responsible for regulating the commodity derivatives markets, including the futures and options markets. Its authority stems from the Commodity Exchange Act, whose definition of "commodity" reaches beyond physical goods to intangible assets.
This is why BTC and ETH can be treated as commodities under existing U.S. law, with the CFTC having regulated their futures markets for years.
However, the CFTC’s authority over commodity spot markets is more limited, though it still holds the authority to police fraud and market manipulation. The pending CLARITY Act would expand the CFTC’s role, giving it exclusive jurisdiction over digital commodity spot markets and requiring exchanges and brokers that handle those assets to register with it.
The Role of the SEC
On the other hand, the SEC oversees securities. For much of the past decade, the SEC and CFTC have held overlapping and sometimes contested jurisdiction over cryptocurrencies, which left many digital assets in a regulatory gray zone.
In 2026, the SEC, joined by the CFTC, released a statement describing how federal securities laws apply to digital assets, marking a shift away from years of case-by-case enforcement toward a real framework.
The release set out a five-category token taxonomy. One of those categories is digital commodities, defined as assets whose value comes from the workings of a blockchain, and from market supply and demand, rather than from the managerial efforts of others. Digital commodities are treated as non-securities under the joint interpretation.

title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei responds: doesn’t oppose open-weight models, but fears Chinese AI
summary: Anthropic founder and CEO Dario Amodei made his views clear about open-weight models and China's growing AI capabilities.
full_text:
Anthropic founder and CEO Dario Amodei responded on Monday afternoon to murmuring in the industry that his company somehow supports efforts by the U.S. government to ban open-weight Chinese models, or possibly open-weight models generally.
“Anyone who has read my past writing should know that I don’t regard such bans as a useful measure, but let me state it clearly so that there is no doubt: Anthropic has never advocated for a ban on open-weights models,” he wrote, emphasis his own.
His response came after Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang took to X (his first post on the platform) to share an open letter on Friday in which Nvidia and a long list of other AI companies including Hugging Face, Meta, Microsoft, Mistral, and Nvidia urged policymakers not to impose broad “premature restrictions” on open-weight AI models.
While that letter did not mention China specifically, the debate in the industry has centered on allegations that Chinese AI labs are growing in capability often by stealing intellectual property from their American counterparts. One method is distillation, where an AI bombards another model with prompts to learn how it works.
Amodei said in the blog post published Monday that he views open-weight models as falling into a different bucket than the threat China poses. “Open-weights models that don’t have dangerous capabilities are a public good: they don’t cost anything besides the compute needed to run them, and they provide value to businesses, developers, and researchers.”
Amodei said in his post that he has longstanding fears about AI, but businesses using open-weight models, even ones from China, are not among them.
His fear is that “authoritarian governments” will build models that are more powerful than those in the U.S. to achieve “permanent military superiority” and/or use AI to repress their own people. He said the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) isn’t the only authoritarian government he’s concerned about, but it is the “most capable.”
Amodei also said he fears AI will enable “biological attacks” not just cybersecurity ones. And, in his view, open-weight models are more dangerous in those scenarios because it’s difficult to apply guardrails to them or monitor their usage. He also noted, citing a UK AI Security Institute report, that once open-weights are released they cannot be withdrawn
This runs counter to what open source advocates argue: that access to powerful open models not controlled by a single entity helps defenders protect themselves.
Amodei listed actions he believes would thwart China, including restricting its access to powerful chips (which has been a longstanding U.S. policy) and calling for a formal crackdown on distillation. The U.S. has threatened sanctions against China if it determined there was IP theft involving U.S. models.
Interestingly, Amodei also said he supports growing efforts, some led by the U.S., to create a model safety testing organization, especially if the entire world, including China, agreed to submit to it.
“I think this idea is actually close to a consensus: I have been heartened both that the Trump administration has moved in this direction in recent months, and by recent industry proposals that would apply such testing to the most capable models regardless of their country of origin or whether they are open or closed (while exempting less capable models, such as those from startups and academia, entirely),” Amodei wrote.
“Note that to be effective,” he added, “testing would need to be global, which means even the CCP would need to be on board. I think this may actually be possible … limited cooperation around preventing AI biological weapons may be possible because it is in China’s interest too.”

title: 美伊連三天停火》川普喊很可能達成協議，布蘭特原油回落 85 美元水平
summary:

〈美伊連三天停火》川普喊很可能達成協議，布蘭特原油回落 85 美元水平〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
美伊連續第三天未爆發空襲，布蘭特原油回落，川普稱談判「很可能」達成協議。
（前情提要：中東戰火降溫！美軍暫停轟炸伊朗，川普轉向推動荷姆茲海峽停火談判）
（背景補充：高盛警告油價暴漲：極端情況布蘭特原油將突破每桶120美元）
布蘭特原油從上週末的接近 100 美元，已重摔 15%，收在 85 美元附近。伴隨油價走跌的，是戰場上難得的平靜，美軍已連續第三天沒有對伊朗發動空襲，德黑蘭也同步收手，暫停了對科威特等波灣鄰國的攻擊行動。
川普喊接近協議，德黑蘭卻說沒這回事
這不是川普第一次把話說得很滿。他過去已多次宣稱和談露出曙光、即將拍板定案，但戰事仍反覆延續，外界至今說不準美伊雙方究竟有沒有真的坐上談判桌。
稍早他在專機空軍一號上再度表態，說法是伊朗之所以願意坐下來談，是因為美軍持續施加猛烈軍事壓力；如果談判順利收場，雙方就繼續談下去，一旦破局，美軍便會恢復先前的行動節奏。連帶著，他先前多次揚言要對伊朗發動大規模打擊的強硬語氣，這回也暫時收了起來。
可是德黑蘭給出的版本卻完全不同調。伊朗外交部發言人巴格赫裡稍早強調，眼下並沒有任何正式磋商在進行，頂多是居中調解的第三方，把美方對當前局勢的看法帶到伊朗這邊而已，其餘細節他並未鬆口。
荷姆茲海峽：水雷不清，航道就通不了
知情人士透露，伊朗與阿曼官員上周末在德黑蘭會晤後，持續協商恢復荷莫茲海峽航運，方案之一是重新開放海峽中間航道。中間航道自 2 月底衝突爆發以來幾乎沒有船隻敢走，油輪多半改繞行貼近伊朗海岸的北側航道，或靠近阿曼飛地穆桑達姆的南側航道。
若想重開荷姆茲海峽的中間航道，有個重要關卡是海底的水雷，這條路線很可能早已被伊朗佈雷，非得先完成排雷作業不可。
英、法等歐洲國家已鬆口表態，只要安全條件到位，願意領頭協助清除水雷。阿曼一方的談判代表對外發布的訊息偏樂觀，認為未來幾天有機會看到進一步的成果，但同時也坦言，最終能不能敲定協議，誰都無法打包票。

summary:
亞股週二同步重挫：南韓 KOSPI 再次觸發熔斷、台股摜破 1,700 點、日股同步跳水。本週三聯準會利率決議 […]

〈韓股又熔斷、日經跳水 4%、台股大跌 1800 點失守 42k，權值股大逃殺〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
亞股週二同步重挫：南韓 KOSPI 再次觸發熔斷、台股摜破 1,700 點、日股同步跳水。本週三聯準會利率決議與核心 PCE 資料將是下一個觀察重點。
（前情提要：臺股崩盤 2953 點創史上最慘！AI 去槓桿海嘯襲全球，比特幣反而相對堅挺）
（背景補充：韓國股市單日暴跌逾8%！KOSPI觸發全年第七次熔斷，SK海力士領跌13%）
亞股今（28）日同步失血：南韓 KOSPI 盤中大跌超 8% 再次觸發熔斷機制，股票交易暫停 20 分鐘；日股重挫 2700 點跌超 4%，台股加權指數目前跌幅也超過 4%，失守 42,000 點。
權值股同步遭到血洗：臺積電（2330）盤中一度跌至 2,270 元，重摔 80 元，跌幅超過 3%。聯發科 3,445 元（跌 235 元、6.39%）、臺達電 1,655 元（跌 100 元、5.70%）、鴻海 246.5 元（跌 6.50 元、2.57%）、日月光投控 575 元（跌 33 元、5.43%）。
這波賣壓的引信，從前一晚的美股收盤就已點燃。費城半導體指數（費半）當晚下跌 2.2%，起因是投資人開始質疑科技巨頭砸進 AI 基礎建設的資本支出，究竟能不能換回相應的回報。
比特幣同步回落，但跌幅比震央小得多
撰稿當下，比特幣報 63,258 美元，24 小時下跌 3.06%；以太幣報 1,875.17 美元，跌幅 3.66%。
如果把這波亞股跌幅擺在一起看：KOSPI 重挫 8%、台股盤中跌超 4%、日經下殺 4.6%、比特幣的跌幅相對波動較小。
不過比特幣的反彈底氣也不足。BTC 剛從上週五反彈近 4%，盤整於 65,000 美元附近，以太幣一度觸及近兩個月高點；但比特幣期貨未平倉量並未同步走高，顯示這波反彈缺乏槓桿買盤支撐。
Nansen 資深研究分析師 Nicolai Sondergaard 指出：「市場保持區間震盪，缺乏強勁買家。」他認為近期反彈「缺乏持續上漲前通常會見到的買進信心」，並將下檔目標區間看向 52,000 至 58,000 美元。

title: 一張寶可夢卡賣 5.17 億元！日本政府成立卡牌議員聯盟：偽卡、囤貨、洗錢一次盯
summary:
一張稀有寶可夢卡以約 1,600 萬美元售出，讓日本執政黨坐不住。跨派系議員聯盟「卡牌議連」7 月 23 日在 […]

〈一張寶可夢卡賣 5.17 億元！日本政府成立卡牌議員聯盟：偽卡、囤貨、洗錢一次盯〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
一張稀有寶可夢卡以約 1,600 萬美元售出，讓日本執政黨坐不住。跨派系議員聯盟「卡牌議連」7 月 23 日在國會掛牌成立，會長木原誠二點名偽造、囤積轉賣與洗錢三大課題。
（前情提要：寶可夢卡 1,650 萬鎂破世界紀錄！Logan Paul 爽賺 800 萬，NFT 碎片化投資者卻血本無歸）
（背景補充：Bankless：寶可夢卡牌代幣化平台一覽）
一張寶可夢卡，今年 2 月以約 1,600 萬美元（約合新臺幣 5.17 億元）的天價售出，賣家是網紅 Logan Paul。這個數字讓日本執政黨自民黨坐不住：7 月 23 日，一個專門盯著集換式卡牌市場的跨派系議員聯盟「トレーディングカード振興議員連盟」（下稱卡牌議連）在國會內舉行設立總會，會長木原誠二直言，集換式卡牌是「能在世界上競爭的產業」，但囤貨、轉賣、偽造與洗錢的問題已經浮上檯面。
議連掛牌，木原誠二點名三大課題
卡牌議連的設立總會由木原誠二主持，眾議院議員石原正敬在會上報告議連運作方向，神田潤一則就監管方向提出討論。木原誠二在會上把卡牌市場的風險歸納為三大課題：
第一，偽造品流通，目前幾乎全靠民間鑑定機構把關
第二，以轉賣為目的的大量囤積
第三，洗錢遭濫用，根本原因是卡牌缺乏個體識別碼，一張卡從印刷到易主全程無法追蹤。
數字說得更直接。依日本經濟產業省統計，這塊生意 2021 年度還只有 1,776 億日圓，到 2025 年度已經衝上 3,384 億日圓，四年翻了將近一倍，折算約 21 億美元。錢一多，紙片的性質就跟著變：自民黨內部的評估寫得很白，這些卡片早已跨過消費品的界線，買賣行為愈來愈接近在操作一項金融資產。
定價權握在美國手上
更尷尬的一層在後面。寶可夢、遊戲王都誕生在日本，可是一張卡最後能喊到什麼價，得看太平洋另一端的美國鑑定商 PSA 給幾分：分數決定行情，行情決定流動性，連帶決定這張卡能不能被當成資產拿去抵押、拆分或交割。
議連聽取業界意見後抓到的痛點正是這個結構：IP 長在自家，認證與估值的話語權卻握在別人手上，日本對自己內容產業長出來的資產，幾乎沒有喊價的餘地。
收藏品的金融化，加密圈其實不陌生
當一件實體收藏品因為單價夠高、易於攜帶、能跨境流通、又缺乏個體識別碼而被拿來洗錢，監管單位的反應路徑其實跟加密貨幣如出一轍：先是任由市場野蠻生長，等到規模與案件都大到無法忽視，才回頭補上牌照、揭露義務與交易追蹤機制。
日本這次選擇提早布局，一方面是想在偽造與洗錢問題失控前先卡位，另一方面也是不想讓卡牌重蹈加密貨幣人才出走的覆轍。
值得玩味的是「定價權外流」這一段，日本擁有 IP，估值卻交給美國的 PSA，某種程度上就像現實世界資產代幣化最常被提到的痛點：內容或資產在地，但誰來當真相仲裁者卻握在別人手上。
卡牌議連線下來會持續聽取製造商與鑑定業者的意見，最終端出的政策草案，會不會也成為其他國家處理「收藏品金融化」的參考模板，值得繼續觀察。

title: 薩爾瓦多 2027 大選反對黨候選人出爐，布格磊比特幣策略面臨政治考驗
summary:
薩爾瓦多兩大反對黨正式提名 2027 年 2 月總統大選候選人，兩位候選人均把布格磊的比特幣策略標記為財政失敗 […]

〈薩爾瓦多 2027 大選反對黨候選人出爐，布格磊比特幣策略面臨政治考驗〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
薩爾瓦多兩大反對黨正式提名 2027 年 2 月總統大選候選人，兩位候選人均把布格磊的比特幣策略標記為財政失敗。
（前情提要：薩爾瓦多砸 1 億美元抄底 1090 枚比特幣，總持倉量直衝 7500 枚 BTC）
（背景補充：比特幣總統布格磊成功連任！薩爾瓦多穩固 BTC 法幣化道路）
薩爾瓦多兩大主要反對黨已正式提名 2027 年 2 月總統大選候選人，布格磊（Nayib Bukele）的第三任期與比特幣策略迎來政治挑戰。民族共和聯盟（ARENA）推舉前議員 Maytee Iraheta，法拉本多・馬蒂民族解放陣線（FMLN）則提名醫師兼工會領袖 Rafael Aguirre。
兩位候選人均反比特幣策略
兩位候選人對布格磊的比特幣策略皆持批評態度，ARENA 稱之為「財政失敗」，FMLN 同樣認為每日購入比特幣是一種浪費公帑的行徑。
布格磊所屬的新思想黨已於本月完成提名，搭檔為現任副總統 Felix Ulloa。ARENA 這次也創下歷史——Iraheta 與搭檔組成該黨首個全女性競選組合。
94% 支援率下的隱憂
兩黨在立法議會席次有限：ARENA 僅 2 席，FMLN 自 2024 年以來已無任何席次。布格磊近期民調支援率高達 94%，根據一項調查，只有 2.2% 的薩爾瓦多人認為比特幣是他最大的失誤。
比特幣已非法定貨幣，但購幣計畫持續
薩爾瓦多已在 2025 年 2 月與 IMF 達成 14 億美元貸款協議，取消了企業必須接受比特幣的強制性規定，美元重新成為唯一官方貨幣。不過，國家比特幣辦公室仍持續執行「每日約 1 枚 BTC」的購幣計畫。
根據國家比特幣辦公室追蹤器資料，截至 7 月 27 日薩爾瓦多比特幣持倉已達約 7,730 枚 BTC，較一個月前約 7,700 枚的持倉穩步增長，確認布格磊「每日 1 BTC」的承諾仍在執行。
下屆總統將繼承的賭注
比特幣現價在 65,300 美元附近，距 2025 年 10 月創下的 126,000 美元高點已下跌近半。今年早些時候，價格回撥已使國家持倉蒸發近 3 億美元。IMF 多次警告比特幣策略存在財政與治理風險，並指出該策略尚未顯著改善無銀行帳戶薩爾瓦多人的金融包容性。

title: 紐約檢察長警告：CLARITY 法案削弱州級加密監管，5 年詐騙損失近 5 億美元
summary:
紐約檢察長莉蒂亞・詹姆斯向參議院提交書面證詞，警告聯邦《CLARITY 法案》可能覆蓋州級監管權，並呼籲國會要 […]

〈紐約檢察長警告：CLARITY 法案削弱州級加密監管，5 年詐騙損失近 5 億美元〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
紐約檢察長莉蒂亞・詹姆斯向參議院提交書面證詞，警告聯邦《CLARITY 法案》可能覆蓋州級監管權，並呼籲國會要求加密平台遵守反洗錢、消費者保護與利益衝突規範。
（前情提要：快訊》美參院共和黨推新版《Clarity Act》清晰度法案，五大監管亮點一次看）
（背景補充：川普、參議員同步施壓 CLARITY Act 迎 8 月休會衝刺，執法單位雙管齊下）
紐約州檢察長莉蒂亞・詹姆斯（Letitia James）週一向參議院常設調查小組提交書面證詞，警告聯邦《數位資產市場清晰法》（CLARITY Act）可能剝奪州級監管權，並呼籲國會為加密平台建立更嚴格的消費者保護規範。詹姆斯在正式宣告中詳細列出 5 項核心要求。
她指出，聯邦法案若直接由商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）接管監管，地方執法單位將失去調查詐騙與追緝不法平台的工具。
3 年申訴翻三倍，5 年損失近 5 億美元
根據詹姆斯的統計，紐約州過去 3 年收到的加密詐騙申訴數量翻了 3 倍，過去 5 年累計損失接近 5 億美元（約 15 億新臺幣）。她指出，這只是民眾主動報告的部分，實際數字可能更高。
相比之下，歐洲的監管模式是「先定規則、後查違規」。歐盟《加密貨幣監管法規》（MiCA）規定交易所每筆交易需有 1:1 資產證明，而美國目前依賴的是各州自行制定的法規，標準不統一。
5 大要求：反洗錢、消費者保護、利益衝突全涵蓋
詹姆斯在證詞中列出 5 項核心要求：
- 反洗錢規範：加密平台需遵守反洗錢（AML）、瞭解客戶（KYC）及網路安全標準，並監控可疑交易與市場操縱。
- 財務責任：平台未保護消費者時應承擔財務責任，讓平台有動機做好風控。
- 禁止混幣器換匯：禁止使用混幣器或無法追蹤的加密貨幣兌換美元，確保資產流動透明。
- 保留州級法律：維持現有的州級貨幣傳輸、商品與證券法，不讓聯邦法案自動取代地方規定。
- 利益衝突禁令：禁止有加密產業財務利益的選舉人或官員參與監管決策。
州級監管的重要性
詹姆斯強調，州級監管並非多餘。她說：「每個州的市場結構、消費者人口和詐騙模式都不一樣。單一聯邦標準無法覆蓋所有情況。」
以加州為例，加州證券委員會（COS）在 2025 年對 3 家加密平台開出 450 萬美元罰單，理由是未保留交易記錄。如果聯邦標準統一，加州可能失去這些執法工具。
CLARITY 法案的最新進度
《CLARITY 法案》目前已在參議院銀行委員會透過，預計 7 月底前送交全院表決。不過，參議院多數黨領袖已警告兩黨在細節上仍有分歧，8 月休會前能否透過仍不確定。
這次紐約檢察長的證詞，是執法單位對法案內容的第一次公開提醒。如果最終版本只靠一個 CFTC 統一監管，州級執法工具可能消失，民眾面臨的詐騙風險可能進一步上升。

full_text:
比特幣今（28）日回檔至6.3萬美元、以太坊跌破1,880美元，全網爆倉6.1億鎂，恐懼指數回落至29，市場情緒持續低迷。
（前情提要：比特幣站回6.5萬美元、以太坊衝破1940「爆倉2.1億鎂」，恐懼指數回升30）
（背景補充：以太坊甦醒？ETH/BTC 匯率創 3 個月新高，Arkham：歷經四年 80% 跌幅後強勢回歸）
比特幣今（28）日延續回檔走勢，昨晚美股收盤漲跌互現後，加密市場進一步下探。比特幣一度觸及63,457美元，創近一週低點，以太坊同步失守1,880美元關卡，唯獨兩大資產近14天均未破前低，多頭格局尚未完全瓦解。全網過去24小時爆倉達6.1億美元，多頭慘遭清洗，恐懼貪婪指數回落至29，市場情緒持續低迷。
宏觀與催化劑
美股週一（27日）收盤漲跌互現，道瓊工業指數小漲0.51%收52,210點，標普500指數持平於7,413點，那斯達克指數微跌0.18%收24,932點，市場關注聯準會本週利率決議。川普再施壓Fed降息，稱美國借貸成本應為全球最低，此訊息為風險資產提供一定支撐，但加密市場反應冷淡。
其他幣種表現
主流幣種全面走弱，SOL報73.7美元，24小時跌幅3.42%，逼近近14天低點73.68美元；XRP跌勢最深，下跌4.49%至1.0587美元，續創14天新低。整體市場缺乏利多催化，資金持續流出風險資產。
市場情緒與前瞻
恐懼貪婪指數今日報29，較前一日30回落1點，延續近8日的低迷區間（25-33），市場情緒維持謹慎。比特幣近14天高點為66,803美元（7月21日），低點62,474美元（7月14日），目前處於區間中下緣；以太坊14天高點1,967美元（7月27日下午），低點1,779美元（7月14日），短線仍有下行壓力。

title: Bitmine 再掃 1 萬枚 ETH！持倉達 579 萬枚，Tom Lee：以太幣動能強化
summary:
Bitmine 上週再添近 1 萬枚以太幣，總持倉達 579 萬枚（約 4.8% 全網供應量），其中 85% […]

〈Bitmine 再掃 1 萬枚 ETH！持倉達 579 萬枚，Tom Lee：以太幣動能強化〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Bitmine 上週再添近 1 萬枚以太幣，總持倉達 579 萬枚（約 4.8% 全網供應量），其中 85% 已投入質押營運。公司預估年化質押報酬約 2.99 億美元，chairman Tom Lee 指出 ETH/BTC 比值已創三個月高點。
（前情提要：Bitmine 再砸 1 億美元掃貨 5.1 萬枚以太坊！Tom Lee 喊話：回檔即是買點）
（背景補充：Bitmine 上週再掃貨 4.2 萬枚 ETH！總持倉突破 574 萬枚叩關「5% 供應量」）
Bitmine Immersion Technologies 週一宣布，過去一週內再添近 1 萬枚以太幣（ETH），總持倉達到 579 萬枚，約佔以太坊全網供應量的 4.8%。
公司同時揭露，約 490 萬枚 ETH（佔持倉 85%）已透過自營驗證者營運投入質押。Bitmine 預估，當所有以太幣全面部署至質押基礎設施與合作驗證者後，年化質押報酬將達約 2.99 億美元。截至 7 月 26 日，公司加密資產、現金與有價證券總計 118 億美元。
ETH 跑贏 BTC，Tom Lee 看多 ETH/BTC 比值
這波買進發生在以太幣跑贏比特幣的行情中。根據 CoinGecko 資料，ETH 過去七天漲約 2.4%，比特幣則微跌約 0.7%。
Bitmine 董事長 Tom Lee 在週一公告中表示，ETH 對 BTC 的比值已攀升至三個月高點，顯示以太幣動能正在強化。
全球最大企業 ETH 寶庫，策略漸與 Strategy 分岔
Bitmine 目前已建立全球最大的企業以太幣庫，僅次於 Strategy 的數位資產總值。不過兩家的積累策略已出現分歧，Strategy 近幾週暫停購買比特幣，轉而透過售股籌措資金；Bitmine 則持續穩定加碼 ETH。
週一 Strategy 宣布透過售股籌得 5.445 億美元，回購 2,500 萬美元優先股，並將美元儲備提升至 37.5 億美元，比特幣持倉維持 843,775 枚。
Bitmine 的「5% 煉金術」目標（控制以太坊 5% 供應量）距離目前 4.8% 已進入最後衝刺階段。若照此節奏，年底前達成目標的可能性不容忽視。

週一，Cross River Bank 正式宣布，將成為 X Money 的銀行基礎設施供應商，為這個嵌入 X 平台的金融服務提供人對人支付、享有美國聯邦存款保險（FDIC）保障的計息帳戶，以及 Visa 簽帳卡。
Cross River 表示，其銀行平台和支付軌道將支撐 X Money 的服務，基礎設施也為未來擴充套件更多金融產品預留空間。
X Money 的「全能 App」路線圖
Cross River Bank 是銀行即服務（BaaS）領域的先驅，透過受監管的銀行平台為金融科技和科技公司提供支付、簽帳卡、貸款和加密貨幣服務。此次合作未提及加密貨幣或穩定幣支援，顯示 X Money 目前仍以傳統銀產業務為主軸。
馬斯克自 2022 年起就多次暗示 X Money 的存在，當時他將收購 Twitter 形容為「打造全能 App X 的加速器」。X Money 在 2025 年 5 月進入內部封測階段，馬斯克當時強調處理使用者存款需要「極度謹慎」。2026 年 3 月，服務擴充套件至有限外部測試。
超過 40 個州的執照布局
截至目前，X 已獲得超過 40 個美國州的貨幣傳輸執照（MTL），並向金融犯罪執法網路（FinCEN）註冊，為平台內的人對人支付掃清監管障礙。
Cross River Bank 此次入場，意味著 X Money 的後臺銀行系統已確定。隨著 P2P 支付、FDIC 保險帳戶和 Visa 簽帳卡三大核心功能上線，X Money 正逐步從「測試版概念」轉向實際營運的金融服務平台。
與臺灣市場相比，X Money 的「全能 App」策略與 Line 的金融生態系（Line Bank、Line Pay、信用卡）高度相似。不同的是，X Money 選擇與傳統銀行即服務供應商合作，而非自行申請銀行執照，這條路線在金融監管上更加穩健。

title: Johnson & Johnson offers up to $5.5bn to settle baby powder lawsuits
summary: The proposed settlement aims to close a years-long legal battle over claims its talcs products cause cancer.
full_text:
Johnson & Johnson offers up to $5.5bn to settle baby powder lawsuits
- Published
Johnson & Johnson (J&J) has offered to pay as much as $5.5bn (£4.14bn) to resolve tens of thousands of lawsuits in the US alleging that its baby powder and other products containing talcum cause ovarian cancer.
The proposed landmark settlement aims to close a long-running legal battle that has weighed on the New Jersey-based healthcare giant for years.
J&J has denied that its talc-based products caused cancer and has changed the formula of its widely-used baby powder.
Erik Haas, the firm's vice president of litigation said on Monday, external that the allegations are "meritless" and that J&J was willing to settle in order to finally resolve the matter.
J&J said the settlement would cover about 69,000 cases, totalling most of the remaining talc-related claims. The firm will offer up to $3bn next year, with no additional payments due before 2028, it said.
The proposal must be accepted by legal firms representing 95% of the ovarian cancer claims in state and federal courts before it can be finalised, the J&J said.
Haas said in a statement that the company is confident that it would have "ultimately prevailed with further litigation" just as it has in the majority of cases heard in court to date.
He added that the proposed resolution "allows the company to put this matter behind it" and enable J&J to "remain focused on its mission to develop medicines and devices that save lives".
J&J's former consumer health business, Kenvue, holds liability for Johnson's baby powder outside North America.
Kenvue - which owns well-known brands including Band-Aid, Listerine, and Calpol - was spun off from J&J in 2022.
Lawsuits against J&J over its talc-based baby powder started as early as 2009.
Earlier in July, a federal court handed the firm a victory by questioning individual plaintiffs' ability to show that talc was the direct cause of their ovarian cancer.
Talc is a natural mineral made of magnesium, silicon, oxygen and hydrogen, known for its soapy feel and is often used in baby powder.
The company has faced lawsuits from consumers and their survivors who claim J&J's talc products caused cancer due to contamination with asbestos.
Talc is mined from the earth and is found in seams close to that of asbestos, which is a material known to cause cancer.
J&J has repeatedly denied the allegations and in its latest announcement said: "Studies show talc is safe, does not contain asbestos and does not cause cancer."
In 2022, J&J said it would stop making and selling its talc-based baby powder around the world.
The announcement came more than two years after it had ended sales of the product in the US.
"As part of a worldwide portfolio assessment, we have made the commercial decision to transition to an all cornstarch-based baby powder portfolio," J&J said at the time.

title: Trump says Iran war talks taking place during lull in strikes
summary: The US president says "there is a good chance that something could happen", as Iran denies direct talks are taking place.
full_text:
Trump says Iran war talks taking place during lull in strikes
- Published
US President Donald Trump has said "there are very friendly negotiations going on" about the conflict with Iran, after the warring sides did not exchange strikes for a third straight day.
He expressed optimism for an end to the war on Monday, telling reporters aboard Air Force One: "I think there's a good chance that something could happen."
However, he warned that Washington would "go back to doing what we were doing" before the pause in fighting if the latest negotiations failed.
Tehran has denied that any direct negotiations are taking place.
Trump said he had decided to pause US strikes on Iran on Friday because the countries mediating between them had asked him to give the talks another chance.
Iran has also halted its attacks.
The pause follows nearly two weeks of daily US strikes and tit-for-tat attacks, effectively unravelling the ceasefire struck in June.
The US military said at the time that its strikes were aimed to "degrade Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz" - a global route for transporting oil.
The price of oil on Monday fell by more than 9% to $87.59 a barrel at one point on hopes the conflict could be de-escalated.
Aboard the presidential plane, Trump also dismissed media reports that after five months of fighting, US ammunition stockpiles were now running low.
"We have a lot of ammunition. We have a lot of the mid-level stuff too, more than we could ever use, no matter what," Trump said. "But we have a lot. I'd like to have more."
He said a "lot of equipment" was being built, in particular Patriots - highly valued US-made anti-ballistic missiles.
"That system is going up. We have a lot," he said.
Meanwhile, White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said the US military "has more than enough munitions, ammo, and stockpiles to serve all of President Trump's strategic goals and beyond, and Operation Epic Fury has exposed what happens when you mess with the United States."
"Even still, the president has urged our defence contractors to constantly produce more made-in-America weapons, which are the best in the world," the spokesperson added.
- As the US pauses the war with Iran, is Trump really running out of weapons? - Published5 hours ago
 
- More than 600 US military service members injured since Iran War began in February - Published13 hours ago
 
The US and Israel launched their strikes against Iran on 28 February. Tehran retaliated by firing missiles and drones on US military bases and other assets located in Gulf states, as well as on targets inside Israel.
In June, Iran and the US signed a memorandum of understanding to stop military operations and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, as well as to reach an agreement to end the war over the following 60 days.
But after Iranian forces attacked tankers in the waterway on 13 July, Washington resumed air strikes against Iran and reinstated its naval blockade of the country's ports.
Tehran retaliated with attacks on US military facilities and bases across the Middle East, killing four American soldiers. The US strikes have since killed dozens of people, according to Iran's health ministry.

title: Fourth heatwave grips parts of UK with 35C forecast
summary: A fourth heatwave of the year is now under way for parts of the UK, with temperatures expected to climb into the mid-30s Celsius later this week.
full_text:
Fourth heatwave grips parts of UK with 35C forecast
- Published
A fourth heatwave of the year is now under way for parts of the UK, with temperatures expected to climb into the mid-30s Celsius later this week.
This latest spell of heatwave threshold-level temperatures is expected to peak on Wednesday in the south-east and east of England.
The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has warned the rising temperatures could increase health risks, particularly for vulnerable groups.
It has issued amber heat health alerts, external for much of eastern England that come into force on Wednesday.
North-south split
The heatwave will not be felt in all parts of the country, with clouds and outbreaks of rain continuing in Northern Ireland, Scotland and northern England.
The hot weather will be focused on central, southern and eastern England on Tuesday thought it may spread slightly northwards and westwards into midweek.
Temperatures in England and Wales are forecast to rise to around 25-32C for the next few days with Wednesday likely to see the peak, with readings of 30-35C across the Midlands, southern and eastern England.
Scotland and Northern Ireland will generally remain cooler and showery with temperatures in the high teens or low to mid-20s Celsius.
Current forecasts suggest that the intense heat across southern and central parts of the UK this week will be short-lived compared to the three previous widespread heatwaves this summer.
Some isolated showers may arrive later in the week.
Heat health alerts issued
July 2026 has been notably hot. The Met Office says the UK mean temperature so far this month is 17.5C, which currently makes it the second hottest of any month on record, behind only July 2006 (17.8C).
The ongoing heat means the East Midlands, East of England, London, and the South East are all under amber alerts heat health alerts from 09:00 on Wednesday until 09:00 Thursday.
The UKHSA warns that significant impacts are likely across health and social care services due to the high temperatures, especially as much of July has seen temperatures well above average by day and by night.
Yorkshire and the Humber, the West Midlands and the South West are all under less severe yellow alerts for the same period.
When will it rain?
An ongoing lack of rain means hosepipe bans are in force for millions of households and dry vegetation has provided fuel for wildfires to burn in a number of areas.
Though there was some rain this weekend, the driest locations - including central, southern and eastern England - saw little, if any, meaningful rainfall.
According to the Met Office, rainfall in England this month is at 4.4mm, one of the lowest levels on record, behind only February 1891 (3.3mm) and tied with June 1925 (4.4mm).
Rainfall levels in Wales, where drought was triggered last week in some parts, are so low that July 2026 is currently the fourth driest of any month since records began.
As this next spell of hot weather develops across England and Wales, the lack of significant rain means dry ground and low soil moisture levels are likely to become an increasing concern.
Wisley in Surrey has been one of the driest locations in south-east England with 40 days of no rain as of 27 July.
Though some isolated showers are expected later in the week, there is no significant rain in the forecast.
You can check the latest for your area on the BBC Weather website or app.

title: Hundreds of thousands of women get morning-after pill via free pharmacy service
summary: Since October, the morning-after pill has been made available free-of-charge at high street pharmacies under a new scheme in England.
full_text:
Hundreds of thousands of women get morning-after pill via free pharmacy service
- Published
Hundreds of thousands of women have used a new, free morning-after pill service at high street pharmacies in England, figures reveal.
The scheme launched in October to improve access and save women from having to book a GP or sexual health clinic appointment.
New NHS figures show that almost 305,000 doses were given out at pharmacies between October 2025 and March 2026.
Meanwhile, the number of women asking pharmacists about going on the regular oral contraceptive pill more than doubled, from around 50,000 to more than 115,000 in the 12 months to February 2026.
Easier to access
The morning-after pill, known as emergency contraception, external, is medication designed to prevent unwanted pregnancies. It usually has to be taken within three to five days of having unprotected sex. The sooner it is taken, the more effective it is.
It works by delaying or preventing the release of an egg, but will only prevent pregnancy if ovulation has not already happened.
Alternatively, women can visit a doctor or nurse to have a coil or intrauterine device (IUD) fitted to prevent pregnancy at any time during their menstrual cycle. To be effective, it needs to be fitted within 120 hours or five days of unprotected sex.
The government said making the morning-after pill available free from pharmacies would end the "unfair" barriers and postcode lottery some women faced - with access varying dramatically depending on where they live.
Under the scheme, women can visit their local pharmacy and have a confidential consultation with a pharmacist or trained pharmacy technician, before receiving the medication on the same day.
Prior to this, women had to book an appointment with their GP, sexual health clinic or pharmacy to get the morning-after pill. Women could also access it privately, as they still can now.
In 2024/25, there were around 150,000 NHS prescriptions for the morning-after pill - far fewer than under the new service.
Dr Sue Mann, NHS National Clinical Director for Women's Health, said the pharmacy service was a "major step forward for women's health", with "no appointment, no waiting and no judgement".
"This service is already making a real impact, particularly for women living in more deprived communities, by making contraception easier to access closer to home," she added.
Women can check online, external to find their nearest participating pharmacy. All pharmacists and pharmacy technicians delivering the service have received specialist training to provide emergency contraception and wider contraceptive care.

title: Why attachment theory is everywhere right now and how it can help you
summary: Attachment theory is everywhere right now, but what is it and how can you use it to improve your relationships?
full_text:
Why attachment theory is everywhere right now and how it can help you
- Published
For Lizzy, relationships always seemed to end the same way. "I would get to a second or third date and find something wrong with them."
Just as things began to feel real, the connection she longed for would suddenly feel uncomfortable, even threatening. And she would pull away.
For years, she couldn't explain why - until she came across attachment theory.
And it was the description of a so-called fearful-avoidant - one of the four attachment styles - which felt strikingly familiar.
It describes someone who wants closeness, but worries that people in their life will eventually reject or abandon them.
"It was like I had found the missing piece to a puzzle that I've been trying to solve for years," Lizzy says.
She is not alone. Attachment theory has exploded into the public consciousness.
On TikTok, videos tagged #AttachmentTheory have racked up hundreds of millions of views.
And in popular culture it's used to explain everything from Marianne and Connell's relationship in the hit book and TV series Normal People to the lyrics of Sam Fender and Olivia Dean's record-breaking number one track Rein Me In.
"The first time I listened to it I started crying," Lizzy says.
For her, the song gave voice to both sides of avoidant attachment: the fear that can make love feel unbearable, and the confusion felt by the partner left behind.
What are the four attachment styles?
First developed in the 1950s by British psychiatrist John Bowlby, attachment theory suggests that the bonds we form with early caregivers shape our expectations of relationships.
If support is consistently available, you are more likely to see others as reliable. If care is unpredictable or emotionally distant, you may develop strategies designed to protect yourself from disappointment or distress.
There are four attachment styles - anxious, avoidant, fearful-avoidant and secure. In simple terms they are defined as follows:
- Anxious attachment is often associated with worries about rejection or abandonment. People with this attachment style may seek frequent reassurance from those close to them and struggle with low self-worth. They can be highly attuned to changes in other people's behaviour. 
- People with an avoidant attachment style prioritise their independence and find it difficult to open up emotionally or rely on others. They may subconsciously view intimacy as a threat to their autonomy and withdraw when relationships become too emotionally close. 
- Those with fearful-avoidant attachment (also known as disorganised) want close relationships but often struggle to feel safe in them. They may seek connection one moment and withdraw the next. 
- Someone who is secure is comfortable with both closeness and independence in relationships. They are generally able to trust others, communicate their needs and seek support when they need it. 
Research suggests that secure people tend to fare better not only in romantic relationships, but across life. They manage stress more effectively, cope better with setbacks like rejection or loss and are better colleagues and managers in the workplace.
And what began as a way to understand relationships is increasingly influencing how people navigate them.
Across social media, attachment styles are used to reassess friendships, make sense of family tensions or rule out potential partners.
And relationship coaches promise to reveal the hidden signs of emotional unavailability in a partner or the ways to heal anxious attachment.
The misconceptions around attachment theory
Dr Pascal Vrticka, an associate professor of psychology at the University of Essex, has spent nearly two decades studying attachment.
He says the theory offers "one of the best explanations" for the differences in how people seek support and connection with others.
And while he's glad to see it reach a wider audience, he worries the way it is interpreted can be "outdated, misinformed and, in the worst case, harmful."
"I think one problem is that people are overgeneralising it and using it in contexts where it might not be the best framework to explain our behaviour," he says.
Part of the issue, he explains, is that initial assumptions around attachment theory have evolved since it was first developed.
Vrticka says one of the biggest misconceptions is that attachment styles are fixed.
Although studies have found that they can show a degree of stability over time, Vrticka says change is possible.
"The good news is that the evidence shows that secure attachment is the most stable. Which means that once you become secure, you tend to stay secure."
He says attachment is often reshaped during periods of transition, particularly during adolescence, when young people begin forming close relationships beyond their family.
Later events in our lives, like entering a new relationship, experiencing a breakup or dealing with bereavement, can also be influential.
But Vrticka says that change is gradual and professional support is likely to be needed for people with more entrenched attachment patterns.
It's that nuance, Lizzy says, which is often lost in discussions of attachment theory.
She says some people can be "quick to assume the worst" and reduce others to labels.
However, while she says people with insecure attachment styles should be viewed with more empathy, she acknowledges the importance of self-awareness.
"For me, I know that my avoidant tendencies are toxic and it would be unfair for me to date someone right now," she says.
But, she adds, that doesn't mean people with insecure attachments are incapable of healthy relationships. "It is on you to acknowledge it and put in the work to heal."
How do you become secure?
Few have played a more influential role in bringing attachment to the mainstream than Dr Amir Levine.
His book Attached, co-written with Rachel Heller, was first published in 2010 and has since sold millions of copies around the world.
But in his latest book, Levine shifts the focus from identifying attachment styles to ask a different question: how do you become secure?
Part of the answer, he argues, lies in what he calls "SIMIs" - seemingly insignificant minor interactions.
A text from a friend asking about your weekend. A smile from a stranger.
"The brain monitors small interactions all the time," Levine says. "That's what attachment is about. It's a monitoring system for safety."
And he says these interactions gradually shape what the brain expects from relationships.
Positive experiences build evidence that people can be trusted and relied upon, helping move someone towards what he calls "secure mode".
But equally, a delayed response or a friend failing to follow through on plans can trigger subtle stress responses in the nervous system.
Importantly, Levine says it's possible to have different attachment styles with different people.
So he encourages people to identify the relationships in their lives that already make them feel safe and understood, and to use them "as a vehicle for becoming more secure overall".
And the idea that security can be built through current relationships reflects a broader shift away from seeing attachment as just the result of childhood experiences.
For some, discovering attachment theory can involve re-examining family relationships, which can potentially lead to resentment. But Levine says "it's not just about where you started, but what happens afterwards".
"If that way of thinking helps you understand yourself and move forward, that's useful," he says.
"But if it makes you feel stuck or damaged, then it's not accurate because people really can change."
Levine also argues that insecure attachments can in themselves be strengths.
He says anxious people are often acutely tuned into relationships, spotting subtle shifts in mood, tone and behaviour that others miss, while avoidant people can be fiercely independent and perform well under pressure.
